rule: Buttons must have discernible text
fix: How to fix: For all UI components: provide an accessible name via <label>, aria-label, or aria-labelledby; use the correct ARIA role (or native HTML element with implicit role); communicate current state and properties: aria-expanded, aria-checked, aria-selected, aria-pressed, aria-invalid, aria-disabled; and ensure all id values are unique so aria-labelledby and aria-describedby resolve correctly. Use native HTML elements wherever possible as they carry built-in accessibility semantics.

rule: Elements must meet minimum color contrast ratio thresholds
fix: How to fix: Ensure a minimum contrast ratio of 4.5:1 for normal text (below 18pt / 14pt bold) and 3:1 for large text (18pt+ or 14pt+ bold) against its background. Use a colour contrast analyser to verify all text. Inactive UI components and decorative text are exempt. Avoid light grey text on white backgrounds.

rule: Links must have discernible text
fix: How to fix: Use descriptive link text that clearly indicates the destination or purpose out of context. Replace "click here", "read more", "more", "here" with descriptive text like "Download Annual Report 2024 (PDF)". Use aria-label or aria-labelledby to supplement vague visible text when changing visible text is not possible.
